search_query: The Regal JD Wetherspoon Cambridge St Andrews Street CAMRA
description: Housed in the art-deco shell of Cambridge's 1937 Regal cinema, this vast Wetherspoon occupies two floors of what was once billed as Britain's biggest pub when it opened in 2000. CAMRA lists it in the Good Beer Guide with four regular ales plus eight to ten rotating guests from brewers such as Adnams, Greene King and Sharp's. A licensed rear patio offers outdoor drinking, while the app-driven food menu keeps lunch and dinner affordable. Friday and Saturday nights bring a DJ from ten o'clock, and TV screens show sport throughout. Expect queues and busy service on weekend evenings in this city-centre landmark.
notes: Sources: jdwetherspoon.com, CAMRA Cambridge (id=1658), camra.org.uk WhatPub. Building purpose-built as Regal cinema 1937. Rear patio garden per CAMRA.

search_query: The Petersfield Sturton Street Cambridge CAMRA
description: Backstreet Sturton Street gained a serious drinking destination when this former White Hart and acclaimed Backstreet Bistro returned to pub life in February 2017. A large L-shaped bar mixes traditional wood and plush furnishings with five handpumps pouring the likes of Barsham, Nene Valley and Adnams, plus keg craft lines from Cambridge Brewing Company. Trust Inns took over from Young's in April 2026. Food runs from modern gastropub menus to Sunday service, with a terrace splitting smoking and non-smoking areas. A quieter snug behind the bar suits smaller groups. CAMRA members enjoy a ten percent discount at this Petersfield neighbourhood favourite.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=50194), camra.org.uk WhatPub, thepetersfield.co.uk. Sold by Young's to Trust Inns April 2026. Previous names White Hart, Backstreet Bistro.

search_query: Dobblers Inn Sturton Street Cambridge CAMRA
description: Genuine backstreet character defines this Wells & Co local near the Grafton Centre, where licensees celebrated twenty-one years in July 2023 and CAMRA crowned it City Community Pub of the Year 2019. Formerly Whitbread's City Arms, the pub retains décor from its CAMRA Investments era and pours Cask Marque-accredited Brewpoint ales. Sport is central: Sky and TNT screens, plus teams for football, cricket, darts, pool and cribbage. A courtyard beer garden with heated smoking area is widely praised. Tuesday quiz nights and occasional cider festivals draw a loyal crowd drawn from every walk of Cambridge life.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1724), camra.org.uk WhatPub, thedobblers.com, inapub.co.uk. Previously City Arms; on site since at least 1871.

search_query: Barley Mow Histon High Street Cambridge CAMRA
description: Histon's village local reopened under new owners Mishah and Chelsea in April 2025 after turnover followed Dore McCann's retirement and a Greene King Hive spell. The dog-leg single bar now pairs an outside bar and pizza oven with Thai curries, Sunday roasts and Italian-inspired dishes using 72-hour dough. An impressively large rear garden and front seating host live bands and DJ nights through summer. Pool has returned alongside craft cocktails and rentable pétanque on the lawn. Greene King IPA remains a regular cask line amid a refreshed draught selection in this revived CB24 favourite.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1614), camra.org.uk WhatPub, hihub.info April 2025 reopening. Was Greene King Hive Dec 2023–2025. Website in progress per owners.

search_query: Red Lion Grantchester High Street Cambridge CAMRA Metropolitan
description: Lavishly thatched and designed by Basil Oliver in 1936, this Grantchester gastropub stands on foundations dating to 1777 when it traded as the Axe & Saw. Metropolitan Pub Company, Greene King's premium wing, runs a polished interior of wainscotting, panelling and mixed flooring around a sturdy wooden bar, with a large restaurant, private dining room and multi-level garden of patio, decking and lawn. Seasonal British menus use local suppliers where possible, with prix fixe lunch offers midweek. Dogs are welcome, and live sport screens for major fixtures. Regional guest ales complement Greene King IPA on the pumps.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1654), camra.org.uk WhatPub, redliongrantchester.co.uk. Present building 1936. Queue already has metropolitanpubcompany.com URL.

search_query: Lion and Lamb Milton High Street Cambridge CAMRA DSH Hospitality
description: More than three centuries of village history underpin this 17th-century Milton inn, reopened in October 2024 under DSH Hospitality after Stonegate sought new tenants. DSH blends British pub classics with Indian, Nepalese, Japanese and wider Pan-Asian dishes in a long opened-out bar with snug fireplace and heated covered patio. A large garden includes children's play equipment, with dogs and families explicitly welcomed. Up to two well-kept cask ales from national brands sit alongside familiar keg lines, with Monday-to-Friday meal-and-drink deals. Free Wi-Fi and a cosy fireplace make it as much a workspace stop as a weekend lunch destination.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge WhatPub, lionandlambmilton.com, Cambridge Independent Sept 2024. Reopened May 2025 with new licensee per CAMRA. Queue URL lionandlambmilton.co.uk may redirect; lionandlambmiltoncambridge.co.uk active.

search_query: Wilbrahams Hall Social Club Great Wilbraham Cambridge bar
description: Nestled inside the Wilbrahams' Memorial Hall complex overlooking the recreation ground, this members' bar serves Great and Little Wilbraham rather than passing trade. The 2016 hall building anchors eighteen community groups and hosts farmers' markets, bridge clubs and village events, with the Social Club opening for coffee mornings, teas and drinks during local functions. Annual membership costs five pounds with forms at the bar. This is a village club rather than a fully fledged public house: CAMRA does not list it among Cambridge pubs, and cask ale is not a focus. Contact the Memorial Hall booking secretary for hall hire enquiries.
notes: Sources: wilbrahamhall.co.uk, wilbrahams.co.uk village site. Village social club inside Memorial Hall; not CAMRA-listed pub. Phone is Memorial Hall booking secretary. Queue URL wilbrahams.co.uk/wilbrahams-hall-social-club/ returns 404.

search_query: Kingston Arms Kingston Street Cambridge CAMRA
description: Tucked off Mill Road, this cosy side-street free house returned in March 2023 when beer enthusiasts Jethro Scotcher-Littlechild and Mark Donachy rescued it from a brief Mediterranean restaurant spell. CAMRA named it Cambridgeshire Pub of the Year 2025 and the city's first Asset of Community Value. Up to seven cask ales including a dark beer, plus four still ciders, fill pumpclips climbing the ceiling above breweriana and historic festival posters. A heated walled garden stays busy year-round. Trad jazz and occasional gigs complement Tuesday cribbage, monthly quizzes and bi-monthly minibus pub crawls. Snacks, pork pies and pop-up kitchen takeovers supply food.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1625), camra.org.uk WhatPub, thekingstonarms.co.uk. Queue lists kingstonarms.co.uk (DNS failed); live site is thekingstonarms.co.uk. Brewery/off licence 1871; full on-licence 1876.

search_query: The Emperor Hills Road Cambridge CAMRA Latin tapas
description: On the busy corridor between Cambridge station and the historic centre, this single-room pub pairs Latin American tapas with cask and keg beers since a 2015 change of hands. Bare boards, smart unfussy decor and a colourful tiled bar front set the tone, while Latin American artwork lines the walls and an upstairs function room handles larger groups. A decent rear patio garden supports alfresco drinking, and alternate Saturday nights bring Latin dance music. Planning permission granted in 2024 will retain only the Hills Road frontage before offices rise behind, though CAMRA expects trading to continue for now.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1729), camra.org.uk WhatPub, Cambridge CAMRA pub news Oct 2024, BBC News planning story. Partial demolition/office rebuild approved; pub expected open meantime.

search_query: The Grapes Histon Road Cambridge CAMRA Greene King
description: Arbury's capacious community local survives from a 1930s build where white-painted wooden beams and stained-glass windows remain the sole original flourishes. Greene King leases the freehold and pours IPA plus two changing guests from the brewery list. Multiple nooks within the open-plan layout hold pool and darts, a jukebox and Saturday-night live music, while Sky screens show sport. Friday breakfasts run from ten until noon, Sunday roasts draw families, and alternate Tuesday steak nights pull regulars. CAMRA named it City Community Pub 2023. Ample parking, wheelchair access and a beer garden reinforce its role as a welcoming neighbourhood hub on Histon Road.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1742), camra.org.uk WhatPub, inapub.co.uk, useyourlocal.com. No official website found. CAMRA City Community Pub 2023.

search_query: The Wrestlers Newmarket Road Cambridge CAMRA Thai Charles Wells
description: One of the last survivors on a Newmarket Road strip that has lost many locals, this Wells & Co house balances serious Thai cooking with a welcome for drinkers only. The well-lit single bar serves authentic pad thai and regional dishes daily from noon until three and five until nine, drawing office lunch crowds and evening diners who keep the handpumps working alongside Bombardier, Broadside and up to four Brewpoint guest ales. Charles Wells reinvented the interior in the 1990s oriental style and removed the pool table to prioritise tables, a strategy that has kept the Wrestlers consistently busy while neighbours closed.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1805), camra.org.uk WhatPub, charleswellspubs.co.uk pub guide. Closed Mondays. Pool table removed in 1990s refurb per retiredmartin.com.

search_query: Lord Byron Inn Trumpington Church Lane Cambridge CAMRA Heartwood
description: Closed since February 2026 for a major refurbishment, this large 17th-century Trumpington inn on Church Lane is set to reopen late that year as The Meadow Lark under Heartwood Collection, with nineteen bedrooms making it the group's first Cambridgeshire pub with rooms. Before closure, an L-shaped bar with low beams, wood panelling and varied floor levels opened onto a large garden, conservatory function room and purpose-built accommodation wing. Byron's Pool and Trumpington Meadows nature reserve sit nearby. Heartwood promises seasonally changing menus and enhanced outdoor dining inspired by skylarks and the surrounding landscape. Previously traded as the Unicorn.
operator: Heartwood Collection (reopening as The Meadow Lark)
notes: Sources: CAMRA WhatPub, lordbyroninn.co.uk, Cambridge Independent Feb 2026, Pub & Bar trade press. Temporarily closed 15/02/2026; expected reopen late 2026 as Meadow Lark with 19 rooms.

search_query: The Poacher Elsworth Brockley Road Cambridge CAMRA
description: Chocolate-box thatched charm marked this Elsworth free house where David and Colleen personally welcomed guests for nearly ten years from their 2016 reopening until final service on 28 February 2026. A single polished room with exposed beams blended homely living-room touches and dining tables, while a redesigned Woodland Garden drew summer drinkers. Home-cooked food, Punch cask ale scheme beers and the proprietors' vocal Siberian huskies Roscko and Alaska built fierce loyalty in a village desperate to keep its pub. The parish council has since lodged a community purchase intention with a district council moratorium on sale, hoping to preserve the Poacher for Elsworth.
operator: David and Colleen (closed; community purchase attempt)
notes: Sources: CAMRA WhatPub (closed 28/02/2026), poacherelsworth.co.uk, Elsworth Parish Council village meeting notice. Closed long-term; community ACV/moratorium in progress.

search_query: Green Man Grantchester High Street Cambridge CAMRA garden
description: Reopened in early 2023 after three years shut and a half-million-pound refurbishment, this 17th-century Grantchester building first licensed as a pub in 1847. Low oak beams frame an L-shaped bar, dining room, log-burner snug and Mediterranean heated terrace with grill and bar reaching down a long narrow garden to footpaths onto Grantchester Meadows—backdrop for the Grantchester TV drama. Chef patron Barry Vera and Star Pubs partners serve contemporary British food from noon, with dogs welcome in bar and garden. Entertainment evenings feature sports personalities and musicians; the terrace seats two hundred. Card payments only.
operator: Barry Vera, Joe Scarborough & Christopher Webb (Star Pubs)
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1744), camra.org.uk WhatPub, grantchestergreenman.com, Cambridge News Jan 2023 reopening. Queue URL failed Firecrawl scrape; grantchestergreenman.com loads. Dogs in bar/garden only, not restaurant.

search_query: Portland Arms Chesterton Road Cambridge CAMRA live music
description: Basil Oliver's 1930s design overlooks Mitchams Corner's gyratory, sheltering one of Cambridge's most important independent live-music venues inside a lovingly panelled main bar with real fire. A smaller room with pool table opens to a courtyard garden, and the National Inventory recognises the historic interior. Oscar's Pizzas supplies burgers and pub favourites in-house while up to six cask lines mix Greene King guests with Milton and local brews, plus real cider outside winter and extensive bottled craft. Soundproofed back-room gigs accommodate two hundred with in-house PA, making the Portland essential to the city's music scene since decades of band nights.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1763), camra.org.uk WhatPub, theportlandarms.co.uk. CAMRA Young Members Pub of the Year 2024. Food by Oscar's Pizzas in-house.
